response.query: How should we design a weighting and expansion method to scale site-level kWh/kg and kgCO2e/kg to provincial and national inventories while propagating sampling uncertainty?

results.title: Uncertainty Analysis of Provincial Carbon Emission Inventories: A Comparative Assessment of Emission Factors Sources
results.content:
Title: Uncertainty Analysis of Provincial Carbon Emission Inventories: A Comparative Assessment of Emission Factors Sources
However, due to differences in activity levels, carbon EF values, and accounting method, there is significant uncertainty in the greenhouse gas emission inventories provided by different countries or regions. In terms of methods, macro-level carbon accounting largely adheres to the IPCC National Greenhouse Gas Inventory Guidelines, employing a top–down approach that estimates emissions through primary energy activity data (AD) and default values following sectoral classifications and subsector disaggregation. Based on energy AD from provincial sectors, an improved MCM with Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) [36] in our study was used to analyze the impact of different EFs (default value, measured EF value, and literature EF value) on the uncertainty of carbon emission accounting, providing a scientific basis for achieving the “dual carbon” goal, formulating targeted emission reduction policies, and fair carbon trading. In addition, the main energy consumed by each sector was different (Figure 1), resulting in carbon emissions calculated based on the literature and IPCC default values for industrial production, thermal power generation, and residential life being much higher than the carbon emissions estimated using measured EF values. In terms of departments, whether using literature EF values, default values, or measured EF values, the uncertainty of carbon emission accounting, in descending order, was industrial production, thermal power generation, residential life, and transportation (Table 3). At a 95% confidence interval, the uncertainties of industrial carbon emissions estimated based on literature EF values, default values, and measured EF values were −7.51–9.85%, −8.51–11.04%, and −7.38–8.71%, respectively. This paper evaluated carbon emissions in Hunan Province from 2016 to 2020 by integrating sector-specific energy activity data from four major sectors—industrial production, thermal power generation, transportation, and residential life—and employing EFs from three distinct sources: direct measurements, IPCC default values, and estimates from the academic literature. The analysis revealed consistent overestimation of the provincial carbon emissions when literature-based and IPCC default values were used, compared with estimates generated from empirically measured EFs. These discrepancies were primarily attributed to the variations in EF values associated with industrial production and thermal power generation—the two sectors most sensitive to EF choice.

results.title: N2O EMISSIONS FROM ADIPIC ACID AND NITRIC ...
results.content: Good Practice Guidance and Uncertainty Management in National Greenhouse Gas Inventories N20 Emissions from Adipic Acid and Nitric Acid Production 183 N 2O EMISSIONS FROM ADIPIC ACID AND NITRIC ACID PRODUCTION ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS This paper was written by Heike Mainhardt (ICF Incorporated) and reviewed by Dina Kruger (USEPA). ABSTRACT Nitrous oxide (N2O) is generated as a by-product during the production of adipic acid and nitric acid. The main use for adipic acid is as a component of nylon-6/6; thus production trends are closely correlated with nylon consumption trends. The Revised 1996 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories (IPCC Guidelines) outline a straightforward method for estimating emissions from both adipic acid and nitric acid, in which an emission factor is multiplied by production data. If periodic sampling is not feasible, the IPCC provides default emission factors for both adipic acid and nitric acid production.

Title: How many Kg of CO2 does an Electric kWh emit in Italy? [Data 2025].
# CO2 emissions per kWh electricity in Italy: calculation and updated emission factors [2025]. Find out how to calculate the kg of CO2/kWh in Italy with the updated emission factors. ## CO2 emissions per kWh electricity: why is it important to calculate them? The **CO2 emissions per kWh electricity** are an important figure when calculating the **carbon footprint of a company**, i.e. all direct and indirect emissions associated with its activity. To calculate CO2 emissions per electrical kWh, it is necessary to use a **CO2 / kWh conversion factor**. ## Methods for calculating electricity CO2 emissions. Reducing CO2 emissions per kWh of electricity is one of the key actions to achieve carbon neutrality. The calculation method *location-based* estimates the CO2 emitted per kWh using the **energy mix of the national electricity grid**. For this reason, the location-based approach **uses a national average emission factor**, calculated on the basis of the energy mix. The calculation method *market-based* estimate **how much co2 is produced per 1 electric kWh based on the characteristics of the** **electricity supplier** chosen by the company. With the market-based method, you can **reduce CO2 kg per kWh of electricity through the purchase of Guarantees of Origin (GO)**, without changing the total energy consumption. By producing electricity on site, you reduce the withdrawals from the grid, and you can be sure that the **electrical kWh consumed have zero CO2 emissions**. ## CO2 emission factors of electricity in Italy. To calculate the CO2 equivalent emitted by electricity, we use **emission factors**. ## Carbon Footprint - Food Industry ISPRA emission factors 2024 (location-based CO2 emissions). The location-based emission factors for the Italian electricity grid are manifold. In the method *market-based*, the emission factor **depends on how much purchased energy is covered by Guarantees of Origin (GO), and how much is not.**. * **Energy covered by GO:** In this case, an emission factor of **0 kg CO2 per kWh electricity**, as it comes from renewable sources. ## How to reduce CO2 emissions per kWh electricity. **Reducing CO2 emissions per electrical kWh** in Italy may seem complicated, but there are several effective solutions.
